title: Cognitive bias in large language models: Cautious optimism meets anti-Panglossian meliorism

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model performance on reasoning tasks like the Wason selection task and natural language inference to measure the influence of prior knowledge versus formal logical reasoning.
Testing models on content-free dummy descriptions after training on imbalanced datasets (e.g., drug-drug interactions) to measure deviations toward the most frequent training class.
Prepending tempting but incorrect 'anchor' code strings to code generation prompts (e.g., HumanEval dataset) to observe if models adjust their outputs toward the provided anchor.

Presenting equivalent decision-making scenarios, such as the Asian disease problem, using either positive (gain) or negative (loss) framing to measure shifts between risk-aversion and risk-seeking behavior.
